purpose: Define the complete, compilable, verbatim shape and observable serde contract of monokl's result/diagnostic primitive cluster -- CodeBlock, RankedBlock, ParentContext, Diagnostic, DiagnosticKind, and LineHit -- per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 4 (lines 454-603), so a developer implementing types.rs, the ranking pipeline, or any command that emits diagnostics never has to guess a field, a derive, a serde mechanism, or which of these six types can even appear in JSON at all. Three of the six (RankedBlock, ParentContext, LineHit) cannot be fully treated as symmetric with the rest of this project's locked types: RankedBlock and ParentContext derive Serialize only (no Deserialize -- they are never a request body, never round-trip), and LineHit derives neither (it has no JSON contract whatsoever; using it anywhere a Serialize/Deserialize bound is required is a compile-time failure, not a runtime one). RankedBlock additionally introduces this project's first use of #[serde(flatten)], a mechanism not covered by any prior track's serde-tagging findings (internal tagging, adjacent tagging, or plain field renaming) -- its own six fields and CodeBlock's eight are merged into one flat JSON object with no wrapper key, and this spec verifies by construction that none of the fourteen resulting keys collide. DiagnosticKind's #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")] is this project's first occurrence of that specific rule rather than "camelCase" -- for its three current single-word variants the two rules happen to produce identical output, and this spec states precisely why that is a coincidence of this enum's variant names, not evidence the two rules are interchangeable.
scope: CodeBlock (8 fields, its two-tier Vec-attribute pattern), RankedBlock (an internally-flattened, Serialize-only struct wrapping CodeBlock plus 6 scoring/ranking fields), ParentContext (a 3-field, Serialize-only struct), Diagnostic (3 fields, Serialize+Deserialize), DiagnosticKind (a 3-variant, lowercase-tagged enum), and LineHit (a 2-field struct with no serde derives at all) -- all verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:454-603. It locks: each type's exact field/variant order, derive list, and serde attributes; RankedBlock's flatten-produced JSON shape and the verified absence of key collisions between CodeBlock's 8 keys and RankedBlock's own 6; the serialize-time behavior of RankedBlock's four f64 scoring fields under non-finite values (NaN, Infinity); DiagnosticKind's lowercase-vs-camelCase distinction and why it is currently unobservable; two unenforced invariants on CodeBlock (line_start <= line_end, and matched_lines entries falling within [line_start, line_end]) that CodeBlock's own Deserialize impl does not validate -- a gap the ranking pipeline's own prose (01-core-architecture.md:1217-1219) already acknowledges defensively (via saturating_sub) but does not close at the type level; and Diagnostic's role as the type that would carry docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 2 High item 3's documented pattern of declared-but-inconsistently-populated diagnostics fields, without resolving which commands actually populate it (a per-command behavioral question, out of scope here).
non_goals: All other Section 4 types not in this cluster -- SymbolKind/Visibility/SymbolEntry (SPEC-003), the dependency/export/JSX/LangData cluster (SPEC-005), SearchOptions/SearchLimits/Language/SearchResponse/SymbolsResult/DependentsResult (a separate, later track), and TsconfigMode/WorkspaceOptions/ExtractRequest (a separate, later track).

Whether any specific monokl command (search, symbols, dependents, inspect, etc.) actually populates its diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic> field with real Diagnostic values -- docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md's cross-cutting pattern documents this as inconsistent and largely unpopulated across the corpus (07 cross-cutting section, and Part 1 finding #1, Part 2 finding #3). This track locks Diagnostic's own shape and states its documented role in that gap; resolving which commands populate it, and how, is each command's own implementation track.

Validating CodeBlock.line_start <= line_end, or that matched_lines' entries fall within [line_start, line_end] -- no source document states either invariant is enforced, and adding validation would be a behavioral decision about the ranking/rank_blocks pipeline that constructs CodeBlock values, not a change to this type's own shape. This spec documents both as unenforced (AC-004); it does not resolve whether they should become enforced.

Whether the ranking pipeline (rank/bm25.rs, rank/boost.rs) should guard against ever producing a non-finite bm25_score/coverage_boost/node_type_boost/final_score before constructing a RankedBlock -- this spec states RankedBlock's own serialize-time consequence if one is ever produced (AC-008); it does not resolve whether the pipeline should prevent that upstream, which is that pipeline's own track's decision.

LineHit's actual consumption inside text_search.rs, or any downstream conversion from LineHit into a serializable type -- this track locks only LineHit's own field shape and its total absence of a serde contract; how it is used is text_search's own track.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: CodeBlock (01-core-architecture.md:454-467) compiles with exactly 8 fields in this order: file: Utf8PathBuf, line_start: usize, line_end: usize, node_kind: SymbolKind, code: String, symbol_signature: Option<String>, matched_lines: Vec<usize>, matched_keywords: Vec<String>. It carries exactly two attribute lines: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] -- no Copy/PartialEq/Eq/non_exhaustive. node_kind: SymbolKind references the enum locked in SPEC-003 (docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:263-284); this track does not re-lock SymbolKind's own shape, only that CodeBlock's fourth field has this type.

Of CodeBlock's 8 fields, file/line_start/line_end/node_kind/code carry no field-level serde attribute. symbol_signature likewise carries no field-level attribute -- despite being Option<String>, its missing-key/explicit-null deserialize leniency comes from Option<T>'s own Deserialize impl (established in SPEC-003 AC-005), and on serialize it always emits its key with a JSON null value when None (no skip_serializing_if), the same always-present-key pattern as SymbolEntry.signature (SPEC-003) and JsxAttribute.string_value (SPEC-005). matched_lines and matched_keywords each carry #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] (01-core-architecture.md:463-466) -- both attributes together, unlike DependencyRecord.bindings (SPEC-005 AC-001), which carries only #[serde(default)] with no skip_serializing_if. Consequence: an empty matched_lines/matched_keywords omits its key entirely on serialize (unlike bindings, which always emits an empty-array key); on deserialize, a missing key for either defaults to an empty Vec via the explicit #[serde(default)] -- required for Vec<T>, per the established finding that Vec<T> gets no implicit leniency the way Option<T> does (SPEC-005 AC-001/AC-011).

CodeBlock's five non-Option, non-defaulted fields -- file, line_start, line_end, node_kind, code -- are required on deserialize: a JSON object omitting any one of "file"/"lineStart"/"lineEnd"/"nodeKind"/"code" fails with a missing-field error naming that field. A "nodeKind" value that does not match one of SymbolKind's 15 camelCase forms (SPEC-003 AC-002) fails with a serde unknown-variant error, per SymbolKind's own contract (SPEC-003 AC-009) -- CodeBlock introduces no new fallback or leniency for this field. CodeBlock carries no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] attribute anywhere in its declaration (01-core-architecture.md:454-467): deserializing a JSON object that includes an extra key not among the 8 named in AC-001 (for example, an object with all 5 required keys plus an unrecognized "extraField" key) succeeds, silently discarding the unrecognized key -- the same unknown-key-tolerant behavior SPEC-003 AC-006 establishes for SymbolEntry. A JSON object where "lineStart" or "lineEnd" holds a negative integer (e.g. -1) fails to deserialize with an invalid-value error, since serde_json's integer deserialization for unsigned target types (usize) rejects negative source values outright -- the same out-of-range behavior SPEC-003 AC-012 establishes for SymbolEntry.line. A "matchedLines" array containing a negative integer element fails the same way and for the same reason, since matched_lines' element type is also usize.

CodeBlock's own Deserialize impl does not enforce line_start <= line_end, and does not enforce that every entry in matched_lines falls within the inclusive range [line_start, line_end]. Both are structurally possible to violate: since CodeBlock derives Deserialize with no custom validation and no field-level constraint carries either invariant, a JSON object with line_start: 100, line_end: 5 deserializes successfully as-is, and a matched_lines value of [1, 999999] deserializes successfully regardless of line_start/line_end's values. This is not a novel gap -- 01-core-architecture.md's own ranking pipeline already flags it in prose: the overlaps_significantly comment (lines 1217-1219) states "nothing enforces that invariant at the type level, so an underflow panic is a real possibility, not a theoretical one," and the same function defends against it internally via saturating_sub rather than relying on any type-level guarantee -- the same gap docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #15 already documents for the structurally analogous ExtractRequest.line_start/line_end. The corpus's one relevant test (integration_search.rs's search_result_has_correct_structure, 01-core-architecture.md:2536, asserting line_start <= line_end) exercises only pipeline-produced CodeBlock values, never a hand-constructed or deserialized one that violates the invariant -- so the invariant currently holds only as an emergent property of the ranking pipeline's own construction discipline, not because CodeBlock's own type contract verifies or enforces it.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The ranking pipeline's own defensive saturating_sub and its comment (01-core-architecture.md:1217-1219) already document this gap in prose -- this criterion states the precise type-level consequence (what CodeBlock's Deserialize will and will not reject) and clarifies that the corpus's one relevant test only covers pipeline-produced values, not adversarial/hand-constructed/deserialized ones, rather than claiming to newly discover the gap. Whether to add validation remains a decision for whichever track owns CodeBlock's construction or deserialize path, per non_goals.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: RankedBlock (01-core-architecture.md:469-480) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)] -- Serialize only, no Deserialize, no Copy/PartialEq/Eq -- and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], with exactly 7 fields in this order: block: CodeBlock (carrying #[serde(flatten)], the sole field-level attribute anywhere on this struct), bm25_score: f64, coverage_boost: f64, node_type_boost: f64, final_score: f64, rank: usize, parent_context: Option<ParentContext>. Because RankedBlock has no Deserialize impl, it can never be parsed from JSON -- it is not, and cannot be used as, a request body or any other deserialize target; no missing-field or required-field framing applies to it the way it does to CodeBlock (AC-003), since there is no deserialize path to be lenient or strict about. Every one of its 7 fields (6 own fields plus the flattened CodeBlock) is unconditionally present in its serialize output except where CodeBlock's own per-field serialize attributes (AC-002) cause omission. parent_context carries no field-level serde attribute -- #[serde(flatten)] on block is the sole field-level attribute anywhere on this struct -- so a RankedBlock with parent_context: None serializes its "parentContext" key with a JSON null value rather than omitting the key, the same always-present-key pattern AC-002 establishes for CodeBlock.symbol_signature and AC-010 establishes for Diagnostic.path.

#[serde(flatten)] on RankedBlock.block (01-core-architecture.md:472) merges CodeBlock's own JSON keys directly into RankedBlock's serialized object at the same level, with no "block" wrapper key anywhere in the output -- the resulting flat object's keys are exactly: file, lineStart, lineEnd, nodeKind, code, symbolSignature (from CodeBlock, per AC-001/AC-002; matchedLines and matchedKeywords present only when non-empty), plus bm25Score, coverageBoost, nodeTypeBoost, finalScore, rank, parentContext (RankedBlock's own 6 fields, per AC-005). None of RankedBlock's 6 own camelCase field names collides with any of CodeBlock's 8 camelCase field names -- verified by direct comparison of the two 6-and-8-element key sets, which share no member. Had a collision existed, JSON serialization of the flattened object would either silently duplicate a key (violating JSON's implicit uniqueness expectation, with map-based JSON consumers keeping only the last-written value) or, depending on the serializer's own collision behavior, fail at serialize time -- this spec states only that no such collision exists in the type as specified, not what would happen if one were later introduced.

#[serde(flatten)] does not alter the serialize-time behavior CodeBlock's own field-level attributes already establish (AC-002): a RankedBlock whose flattened CodeBlock has an empty matched_lines and an empty matched_keywords omits both "matchedLines" and "matchedKeywords" keys from RankedBlock's own flattened output, exactly as CodeBlock's own skip_serializing_if would omit them if CodeBlock were serialized standalone -- flatten changes only where a field's key appears in the object hierarchy (top-level versus nested), not whether that field's own per-field serialize attribute fires.

RankedBlock's four f64 scoring fields (bm25_score, coverage_boost, node_type_boost, final_score) carry no field-level serde attribute and are always present in serialize output. Constructing a RankedBlock whose bm25_score field is set to f64::NAN and serializing it with serde_json produces a JSON object whose "bm25Score" key holds the literal value null (not a numeric literal, and serialization does not fail or panic). The same holds for f64::INFINITY and f64::NEG_INFINITY, and for coverage_boost, node_type_boost, and final_score individually -- each of RankedBlock's four f64 scoring fields exhibits this null-on-non-finite behavior independently when serialized, since JSON has no native representation for non-finite numbers and serde_json's documented Serialize impl for f64 substitutes null rather than failing the whole call. No source document states that monokl's ranking pipeline (rank/bm25.rs, rank/boost.rs) guarantees these four fields are always finite before constructing a RankedBlock; if any of them were ever non-finite, the resulting JSON would silently contain null for that field, indistinguishable on the wire from a genuinely absent value, with no diagnostic raised at serialize time.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The serde_json non-finite-to-null behavior is a documented library fact, not a judgment call in itself, but connecting it to 'no source document guarantees these fields are always finite' is a scope observation this spec makes deliberately -- surfacing a real, currently-unaddressed risk without asserting the ranking pipeline is broken or that a fix belongs in this type-shape track (see non_goals). Stated as a concrete, monokl-scoped construction-and-serialize example rather than a general claim about the library, so a tester can mechanically execute the check without independently confirming serde_json's source.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: ParentContext (01-core-architecture.md:482-488) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)] -- Serialize only, no Deserialize, no Copy/PartialEq/Eq -- and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], with exactly 3 fields in this order: kind: SymbolKind, name: String, line: usize. No field carries a field-level attribute; all 3 are unconditionally present in serialize output. Like RankedBlock (AC-005), ParentContext has no Deserialize impl and therefore no deserialize-side contract of any kind. ParentContext.kind: SymbolKind references the enum locked in SPEC-003 (docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:263-284); as with CodeBlock.node_kind (AC-001), this track does not re-lock SymbolKind's own shape, only that ParentContext's first field has this type.

Diagnostic (01-core-architecture.md:490-496) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")], with exactly 3 fields in this order: kind: DiagnosticKind, path: Option<Utf8PathBuf>, message: String. kind and message carry no field-level attribute and are required on deserialize: a JSON object omitting either "kind" or "message" fails with a missing-field error naming that field. path also carries no field-level attribute; as an Option<T> field with none, it deserializes leniently to None on a missing or explicitly-null "path" key (per the pattern established in SPEC-003 AC-005/AC-010 and reapplied at AC-002 above), and on serialize always emits its key with a JSON null value when None rather than omitting it. Diagnostic carries no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] attribute (01-core-architecture.md:490-496): deserializing a JSON object for Diagnostic that includes an extra key beyond kind/path/message succeeds, silently discarding the unrecognized key, the same unknown-key-tolerant behavior SPEC-003 AC-006 establishes for SymbolEntry.

Diagnostic is the type whose instances would populate every diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic> field across monokl's result types, and it specifically instantiates docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 2, High item 3's documented pattern: "Nearly every Part 2 command declares a diagnostics: Vec<Diagnostic> field but never describes it being populated -- refs, definition, diff, tokens, explain, coverage, data-flow, similar all leave it silently unwired." This is narrower than 07's full cross-cutting silent-data-drop section: Part 1 finding #1 (the dependents/WorkspaceIndex gap) is a categorically different phenomenon -- WorkspaceIndex has no diagnostics field at all ("there's no mechanism at all"), not a Diagnostic-bearing field that goes unpopulated -- and several other cross-cutting instances (e.g. dropped structs/enums, dropped symbols, a missing capability signal) describe other data being silently dropped with no relationship to the Diagnostic type. This track locks Diagnostic's own shape (AC-010) and states its documented role in Part 2 High item 3's specific gap; it does not resolve, for any specific command, whether or how its diagnostics field gets populated -- that is each command's own implementation track's responsibility (see non_goals). A Diagnostic value, once constructed, carries no information distinguishing which command or code path produced it beyond whatever text the caller puts in message -- there is no source/origin field on this type.

DiagnosticKind (01-core-architecture.md:498-504) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] and #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")] -- "lowercase", not "camelCase" (the rule used by every other enum/struct in this and every prior track this session) -- with exactly 3 variants in this order: Degraded, Skipped, Warning. No #[non_exhaustive].

The "lowercase" rule applied by DiagnosticKind's rename_all lowercases a variant name's every character uniformly, with no word-boundary handling of any kind -- a categorically different transform from "camelCase", which lowercases only the leading character and, at the field level, additionally restructures snake_case across underscore boundaries (SPEC-003 AC-002, SPEC-005 AC-013). For DiagnosticKind's 3 actual variants -- Degraded, Skipped, Warning -- "lowercase" produces exactly "degraded", "skipped", "warning": directly verifiable by serializing each DiagnosticKind variant and comparing the output against those three exact strings.

DiagnosticKind carries no #[serde(other)] fallback and no #[non_exhaustive] (AC-012). Deserializing a JSON string value for a "kind" field on Diagnostic (AC-010) that does not exactly match "degraded", "skipped", or "warning" fails with a serde unknown-variant error -- including any camelCase-style value that happens to differ from the lowercase form for a variant that would (per AC-013) diverge under the two rules; no such divergence exists for the current 3 variants, but the enum's deserialize contract rejects anything other than the exact 3 lowercase strings regardless.

LineHit (01-core-architecture.md:599-603) compiles with #[derive(Debug, Clone)] only -- no Serialize, no Deserialize, no PartialEq/Eq/Copy -- and exactly 2 fields in this order: line_number: usize, text: String. This is the only type in this cluster (and, among all types this project has locked so far, one of very few) with no serde derive of any kind: LineHit has no JSON representation whatsoever, and there is no rename_all attribute to state since there is no serde attribute macro on this struct at all. Consequence: LineHit cannot be serialized or deserialized directly, and cannot be a field of any struct that itself derives Serialize or Deserialize without a manual custom implementation. Attempting either produces a compile-time failure, not a runtime failure or a silently-wrong JSON shape: rustc rejects the derive with an unsatisfied-trait-bound diagnostic (E0277) whose message states that the trait bound `LineHit: serde::Serialize` (or `serde::Deserialize`) is not satisfied, naming LineHit specifically as the type missing the required impl. This matches docs/architecture/core-types.md's existing characterization of LineHit as "internal grep-hit representation only"; this track locks the field shape that characterization refers to and confirms no serde derive contradicts it.

linked_research: docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:454-603 (Section 4 types.rs verbatim -- the primary source for all six types in this track); docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md, Cross-cutting patterns section and Part 1 finding #1 / Part 2 finding #3 (the diagnostics-population gap, AC-011) and Part 1 finding #15 (the ExtractRequest line_start/line_end precedent that AC-004 distinguishes CodeBlock's own, previously-unflagged instance from); docs/architecture/core-types.md (LineHit's existing characterization, re-verified rather than transcribed, AC-015); .claude/specs/SPEC-003.json (AC-002, AC-005, AC-009's established camelCase/Option-leniency findings, reapplied); .claude/specs/SPEC-005.json (AC-001, AC-011, AC-013's established Vec-vs-Option and rename-rule findings, reapplied and, for DiagnosticKind's lowercase rule, explicitly distinguished rather than assumed to generalize).
revision_note: First draft, produced with an explicit corner-case checklist worked out per type before any criterion was written (missing/null/wrong-type/extra-field on every deserializable type; boundary and cross-field invariants on CodeBlock; non-finite-float serialize behavior on RankedBlock's scoring fields; the flatten mechanism's exact JSON shape and a direct key-collision check; the lowercase-vs-camelCase rule distinction on DiagnosticKind, including what would change it if it mattered; LineHit's complete absence of a serde contract as a compile-time rather than runtime fact) rather than relying solely on the review pipeline to discover gaps after a bare-transcription first pass, per this session's explicit request for very high rigor and non-happy-path coverage. Every serde-mechanism claim (flatten's key-merging behavior, skip_serializing_if surviving through flatten unchanged, serde_json's non-finite-float-to-null behavior, the lowercase transform rule) was reasoned from documented serde/serde_json semantics rather than assumed by analogy to a previously-verified but structurally different case, consistent with the lesson this project's prior five tracks established the hard way: verified findings do not transfer across structurally different serde mechanisms without being independently re-derived.
reasoning: This track's central technical risks, identified before drafting: (1) #[serde(flatten)] is a genuinely new mechanism for this project (distinct from internal tagging, adjacent tagging, and plain field renaming, all already covered) -- worked out its exact key-merging semantics and explicitly verified no collision between CodeBlock's 8 and RankedBlock's own 6 field names by listing both key sets and comparing them directly, rather than asserting no collision without checking. (2) Three of six types in this cluster (RankedBlock, ParentContext, LineHit) are asymmetric with every type this project has locked so far -- two derive Serialize only, one derives neither -- and every criterion touching them states this explicitly rather than silently applying a deserialize-contract framing (missing-field errors, leniency, etc.) that does not apply. (3) DiagnosticKind's rename_all="lowercase" is a different rule from the camelCase rule reapplied throughout this project's prior four tracks; rather than assume it behaves identically because the observable output happens to match for these 3 variants, this draft worked out the actual rule (uniform lowercasing, no word-boundary handling) and stated precisely when it would diverge from camelCase, so the criterion is honest about coincidence versus equivalence. (4) f64's non-finite-value serialize behavior is a real, checkable serde_json fact this draft states as fact rather than hedges -- consistent with this project's established pattern of drafting confidently and letting the independent verification/exit-gate stages empirically confirm or refute it, rather than pre-emptively softening a claim that may turn out correct. Surfaced two genuinely new corner cases no prior audit pass in this project identified: CodeBlock's unenforced line_start<=line_end and matched_lines-range invariants (AC-004), and RankedBlock's non-finite-score serialize risk (AC-008) -- both flagged as judgment_call:true since deciding whether to resolve them is a scope call this track deliberately defers rather than a settled fact, consistent with this project's non-goals discipline of naming every deferred item explicitly rather than leaving a boundary implicit. Omitted api_surface entirely (empty array) since this cluster has no callable methods -- unlike SPEC-005's LangData::ts()/jsx_elements(), none of these six types define an impl block in the verbatim source. Note on AC-013 (non-binding, not independently checkable against DiagnosticKind as specified): the equivalence between "lowercase" and "camelCase" output for the 3 actual variants is a coincidence of their single-word names, not evidence the two rules are interchangeable in general -- a multi-word variant name, which this spec does not introduce, would diverge ("lowercase" producing e.g. partiallydegraded versus "camelCase" producing partiallyDegraded for a hypothetical PartiallyDegraded variant). Kept out of AC-013's own criterion text per canon-auditor's finding that a claim about a variant this spec does not add is not falsifiable against the type as actually locked.
